title: Practice: Similar Shapes - Area and Volume

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of 4 cm and 10 cm. The area of the smaller triangle is 24 cm squared. What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.explanation: Linear scale factor = 10/4 = 2.5. Area scale factor = 2.5^2 = 6.25. Area of larger triangle = 24 x 6.25 = 150 cm squared.

questions.stem: Two similar cylinders have heights 6 cm and 15 cm. The volume of the smaller cylinder is 100 cm cubed. What is the volume of the larger cylinder?
questions.explanation: Linear scale factor = 15/6 = 2.5. Volume scale factor = 2.5^3 = 15.625. Volume of larger cylinder = 100 x 15.625 = 1562.5 cm cubed.

questions.stem: Two similar shapes have areas 18 cm squared and 50 cm squared. A side on the smaller shape is 6 cm. What is the corresponding side on the larger shape?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor = 50/18 = 25/9. Linear scale factor = sqrt(25/9) = 5/3. Corresponding side = 6 x (5/3) = 10 cm.

questions.stem: Two similar bottles hold 250 ml and 2000 ml. The height of the smaller bottle is 12 cm. What is the height of the larger bottle?
questions.explanation: Volume scale factor = 2000/250 = 8. Linear scale factor = cube root of 8 = 2. Height of larger bottle = 12 x 2 = 24 cm.

questions.stem: The linear scale factor between two similar solids is 3. The surface area of the smaller solid is 20 cm squared. What is the surface area of the larger solid?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor = 3^2 = 9. Surface area of larger solid = 20 x 9 = 180 cm squared. A common mistake is to multiply by 3 (getting 60) instead of squaring the scale factor.
